::: {.content-section}
## What you're seeing

Each spin sits in an external field set by how dark the photograph is at that point, $h_i = h_0\,(2d_i - 1)$ with darkness $d_i$ between 0 and 1. The lattice starts hot and disordered and cools toward the final temperature, so the portrait condenses out of thermal noise.

The coupling $J$ decides the style. When it is weak, the spins are nearly independent and each one points up with probability set by its own field, $\langle s_i \rangle \approx \tanh(h_i / k_B T)$. The density of dark spins then tracks the tone of the photo, which is a stochastic halftone. When $J$ is strong and the temperature is below the critical point, neighbors insist on agreeing, and gradients of tone collapse into flat domains. Near $T_c$, fluctuations appear on every length scale and the picture is never quite still.
:::

::: {.content-section}
## Things to try

- **Switch to time-averaged spins.** Averaging over recent frames turns the halftone into continuous tone, much like an old photogravure.
- **Raise the coupling above about 0.5 at low temperature.** The face turns into a few large domains, and small features like the glasses disappear first: they cost more domain wall than their field is worth.
- **Lower the field strength while the coupling is strong.** Only the largest regions of tone can still pay for their domain walls, so the portrait simplifies toward a silhouette.
- **Try Gibbs.** His portrait has a dark studio background, which dominates the field and makes the face harder to recover. The [denoising note](../blog/posts/2026-09-29-ising-inference.qmd) handles him with a little edge enhancement.
:::

## Credits and source

Portraits of Ludwig Boltzmann (1902) and J. Willard Gibbs (before 1903) are in the public domain, via Wikimedia Commons. The simulation is heat-bath Monte Carlo on a 128 × 160 lattice, written in plain JavaScript: [`ising-portrait.js`](https://github.com/dsuvlu/dsuvlu.github.io/blob/main/assets/ising-portrait.js) and the shared [`ising-core.js`](https://github.com/dsuvlu/dsuvlu.github.io/blob/main/assets/ising-core.js).
:::
